focus_candidate.target_route: A finite command prefix can select either dump mode and carry nested JSON bytes. The entry calls json_loadb first, returns on NULL, and passes only its successful result to json_dumps or json_dump_callback.
focus_candidate.failure_condition: An object with a child at dump depth JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH reaches do_dump's new failure guard when separately constructed, but JSON text that would yield such an object requires a parse_value call beyond the parser's maximum depth. json_loadb returns NULL before either dump call.
focus_candidate.alternative_paths: JSON_DECODE_ANY affects the accepted root type and JSON_DISABLE_EOF_CHECK affects trailing input; neither bypasses parse_value's depth guard. assessment.requirement: The JSON dump operation must be able to receive a supported, over-depth json_t so its clean depth-limit failure can be exercised.
assessment.target_route: A finite command prefix selects a dump mode and supplies JSON text. The entry passes the text to json_loadb, returns if loading fails, and passes only the loaded value to json_dumps or json_dump_callback.
assessment.failure_condition: A constructed nested value can reach do_dump at depth JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH and fail cleanly. JSON text yielding that child requires parse_value beyond JSON_PARSER_MAX_DEPTH, so json_loadb returns NULL before dumping.
assessment.alternative_paths: JSON_DECODE_ANY changes the permitted root type and JSON_DISABLE_EOF_CHECK changes trailing-input handling; neither bypasses parse_value's depth check. Both dump modes use the same loaded value, and the complete entry has no later construction or mutation route.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The source test demonstrates supported clean failure for a constructed over-depth value.
The loader rejects the extra parse depth.
Root and EOF flags leave the failed parse_value result as NULL.
Callback dumping starts do_dump at depth zero.
String dumping delegates to callback dumping.
